placements.why: The envelope describes a mandatory, named onboarding checklist ('the Pallasine checklist') that every new hire completes, with a defined artifact history (replacing a prior wiki page) — this is organizational-process content with no existing strata category to hold it, since strata is currently empty. This names a durable organizational-operations category future onboarding, HR, and process envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact.
placements.title: Organizational process and people-operations as a strategic category
placements.frame: What organizational process, structure, or people-operations commitment does this expression establish, standardize, or reinforce?

placements.title: New hires complete a standardized checklist in their first week
placements.frame: What does the onboarding checklist require of new hires, and how has its content or authority evolved over time?
placements.why: Both segments describe the same subject — a named, mandatory onboarding artifact (the Pallasine checklist) with concrete components (accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift) and a stated supersession of a prior artifact (the old wiki page). This is a directional statement about how onboarding is structured and governed, a subject future onboarding-related envelopes will keep feeding — not a one-time fact, so it earns its own leaf under the newly-minted Organization strata rather than sitting loose or being folded into a fact list.
